podcast.title: Drummer Project (Bass Player)
podcast.body: Patrick Carney joined the indie band Drummer, signed to his own Audio Eagle Records label, where he played bass in the studio. This project was unique in that all its members were drummers from various other bands. "Patrick joined them in the studio where he played bass."

podcast.title: Early 4-track Recorder Owner
podcast.body: Patrick Carney's ownership of a 4-track recorder played a crucial role in the initial stages of The Black Keys' formation. It enabled him and Dan Auerbach to record their first demo, which was essential for Auerbach's aspirations as a singer-songwriter. "Since Patrick had a 4 track recorder, he asked Patrick if he would help him make one of these demos."

xref.title: Formation and Early Independent Success (2001)
xref.body: Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney formed the band in 2001 in Accord, Ohio. They released a series of independent albums that, while generally well-reviewed, received limited attention beyond a dedicated fan base prior to their mainstream breakthrough. "Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney first got together in 2001 in Accord Ohio, and they released a series of independent albums that were generally well-reviewed, but didn't receive much attention outside of a tight circle of fans."

xref.title: Band Tension and Patrick Carney's Divorce (2010)
xref.body: During the period surrounding the recording of *Brothers*, significant internal tension arose between Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney. Patrick acknowledged they were "sick of each other" and maintained separate lives outside of band work. This was compounded by Dan's solo album (made without Patrick's knowledge, which upset him), and Patrick's tumultuous divorce from his wife, Denise. Dan believed Denise was "bad news," and she was accused of cheating, playing mind games, and taking money. Patrick consequently suffered from depression and began drinking, leading the band to the brink of collapse, until he divorced his wife over the phone while the band was in Europe, after which their relationship and the band's dynamic began to improve. "Then there was the drama between Dan and Patrick's wife Denise."

xref.title: "Lonely Boy" Music Video Star
xref.body: Derek T. Tuggle, originally a security guard, achieved unexpected fame as the star of The Black Keys' "Lonely Boy" music video. After an initial video shoot with many extras proved ineffective, Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney noticed Tuggle's distinctive dancing in preview edits and decided to feature him exclusively in a single-shot video, which quickly amassed nearly half a million YouTube views. "It's a single shot of Derek T. Tuggle dancing to the song."

xref.title: Accidental Band Formation
xref.body: Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney, who met around ages 8 or 9 and became friends in high school in Akron, Ohio (both briefly attending the University of Akron), initially planned to record a demo for Dan's solo singer-songwriter pursuits. They invited musician friends to Patrick's basement, but on the appointed day in 2001, only Dan and Patrick appeared, leading them to spontaneously form a duo. "On the appointed day, no one except Dan and Patrick showed up. So that left the two of them to form a band on their own."

xref.title: Akron, Ohio Roots
xref.body: Both Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney hail from Akron, Ohio, having met around ages 8 or 9. They became friends in high school, despite contrasting personalities (Dan as a "jock" and Patrick as a "nerd"), and both attended the University of Akron. Their hometown's historical significance as a tire manufacturing hub and their attendance at Firestone High School are notable local connections. "Dan and Patrick are both from Akron, Ohio."

xref.title: Altercation Between Patrick Carney and Jack White
xref.body: On September 13, 2015, Patrick Carney of The Black Keys encountered Jack White at a New York City bar called Cabin Down Below. Carney, who had never met White before, claimed White attempted to fight him, describing White as a "40-year-old bully." White denied any physical fight, stating he merely asked a question Carney couldn't answer. "Patrick, I've never met Jack White until last night. He came to a bar in New York City, I go to a lot with a few friends and tried to fight me."

xref.title: Altercation with Patrick Carney of The Black Keys
xref.body: On September 13, 2015, Jack White ran into Patrick Carney of The Black Keys at a New York City bar called Cabin Down Below. Carney, who had never met White in person, claimed White tried to fight him, calling White a "40-year-old bully" and saying he inspired Carney to play music as a reaction against such "A-holes." White responded on Twitter, denying any physical altercation, stating he merely asked a question that Carney couldn't answer, and urged him to "speak face to face like a human being." "Patrick, I've never met Jack White until last night. He came to a bar in New York City, I go to a lot with a few friends and tried to fight me."

xref.title: Band Internal Crisis (Brothers Era)
xref.body: During the period leading up to and during the *Brothers* album, Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney faced severe interpersonal conflicts, with Patrick explicitly stating they were not "friends" outside of band work. Tensions escalated when Dan recorded a solo album without Patrick's knowledge, leading to months of silence, and further complicated by drama involving Patrick's wife, Denise, whom Dan disliked. Denise's alleged infidelity, "mind games," and financial misconduct contributed to Patrick's depression and increased drinking, bringing the band close to collapse until Patrick ended his marriage while on tour in Europe, which helped restore the band's stability. "The thing that probably kept the block keys together at this point was some stuff that initially kept them apart."

xref.title: Early Ambition as Singer-Songwriter
xref.body: Prior to the formation of The Black Keys, Dan Auerbach aspired to be a singer-songwriter performing in local bars. His need for a demo tape to secure out-of-town gigs led him to seek Patrick Carney's help, which inadvertently initiated their collaboration. "We had this idea of being a singer-songwriter who played the bars in the area, but the no one would give him any out of town gigs without a demo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up With The Black Keys

xref.title: Early Demo (Holy Grail)
xref.body: The Black Keys' very first demo, recorded by Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney with Gary Fumovar on keyboards, was submitted to numerous indie labels, but only Alive Records showed interest. This demo is now considered a "holy grail" by hardcore fans, though Dan and Patrick themselves deem it "very substandard" and prefer it not to be heard. "That demo, the one they sent out to all these indie labels, is like the holy grail to hardcore block keys fans."

xref.title: Resolution with Jack White
xref.body: Following a public Twitter exchange, Patrick Carney announced that he had spoken with Jack White for an hour, finding him "cool, all good." Jack White then publicly responded to Carney, saying, "From one musician to another. You have my respect, Patrick Carney," indicating a resolution to their conflict. "Talk to Jack for an hour. He's cool, all good. Jack responded from one musician to another. You have my respect, Patrick Carney."
